блукати.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *blǫkati, from *blǫditi (“to err”) + *-kati. Erich Berneker suggested a possible influence from *lǫkъ (“bow”) / *oblǫkъ (“arch”). Grigory Ilyinsky alternatively hypothesized a metanalysis of Proto-Slavic *ob- + *lǫkati (“to bow, to bend”), meaning "to deviate from the path", influenced by the semantically close *blǫditi. Compare Russian блука́ть (blukátʹ), Belarusian блука́ць (blukácʹ), Polish błąkać się.
